1.

Petitioner who is arraigned as accused No.3 has filed this petition under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (for short, 'the Cr.P.C.') to grant him anticipatory bail in Crime No.216/2022 (C.C.No.42/2023) pending on the file of Principal, Civil Judge and JMFC Dharwad, for the offences punishable under Sections 120(b), 409, 420, 201 read with Sections 34 and 37 of the Indian Penal code (for short, 'the IPC').
2.
In support of the petition, petitioner has contented that he is innocent and has not committed the alleged offences.
He is falsely implicated.
The complaint neither directly nor indirectly indicate any evidence against the petitioner.
Without any basis, the concerned Police have implicated him.
Petitioner was produced under body warrant and he was in police custody for five days.
Hence, the presence of the petitioner is not required for custodial NC: 2024:KHC-D:16482 interrogation.
After conclusion of the investigation, charge sheet is filed.
Petitioner is released on bail in the main case at Kalburgi.
The offences are not punishable with death or imprisonment for life.
Petitioner is ready and willing to abide by any conditions that may be imposed and offer substantial surety to the satisfaction of the trial Court and hence, the petition.

3. Learned HCGP submitted oral objections stating that Shri.Chandrahasa T.N, Detective PSI, CCD Division, CID, Bengaluru filed a complaint stating that on 03.10.2021, written exam was held for appointment of 545, PSI (Civil) and there were allegations that using Bluetooth device examination was written by some candidates by copying the answers through Bluetooth.
In this regard, DGP and IG, Karnataka has requested the CCD Cyber crime Division Unit of CID to provide technical assistance.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Consequently, a special team was formed of which complainant is one of the member.
He was directed to investigate in how many centers copying was done NC: 2024:KHC-D:16482 using Bluetooth device.

Accordingly, he has investigated the said aspect at Saint Joseph's High School Centre, Dharwad, and collected cell ID of all the mobile service provider to the said centre and requested all the mobile companies to provide dump data in respect of all the calls made from the cell phones on 03.10.2021 from 00:00:01 to 23:59:59 hours.

sentences.text:
4. When he examined all the data scientifically, he found that on 03.10.2021 from 11 A.M. till 12:30 PM, during the examination of paper one, calls were made from Cell number 81234 01613 to Cell Kashinath Hanumantaraya Chilla vs The State Of Karnataka on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82803110/

436 seconds, and 13 seconds continuously.
Similarly, from Cell number 9980908500 to Cell number 9901245785 one call was made for 65 seconds.

On suspicion, when the complainant examined the details of the above three cell numbers, he found that the tower location of cell number 9901245785 was Hubli Dharwad, Saint Joseph High School, College Road, Dharwad City exam Centre.

sentences.text: Similarly, cell number 8123401613 was coming under the tower location of Kodigehalli, Bengaluru.
6. When the complainant examined the SDR details of the cell numbers, he found that Cell number 9980908500 and 9901245785 was secured in the name of Srimant Satapur.
Cell number 8123401613 is taken in the name of Siddappa Marappa Gondali.
Similarly, cell numbers 9945001015 and 8660031794 are taken in the name of Anil Kumar.
Shrimant Satapur, who has taken the PSI examination has given cell number 9980908500 as his contact number in the application.
In the SDR Cell numbers, 9901245785 is forthcoming as the alternative numbers of 9980908500.

When further, details of cell number 8123401613 were verified, it was found that IMEI NC: 2024:KHC-D:16482 of the phone used with cell number 81234 01613 is 866086039340742, and it is used during the examination time.

The same IMEI number phone instrument is used with Sim numbers 9945001015 and 86600 31794.
7.
Shrimant Satapur has attended the PSI (Civil) examination and secured 95th rank.
He attended the exam from Hubli Dharwad Centre, Saint Joseph's High school, College Road, Dharwad and used cell number 9901245785.
To this cell number, the calls from cell number 8123401613 were made illegally through Bluetooth device.

8. On contacting the informers, the complainant came to know that Srimant Satpur has contacted mediators and paid money and through Bluetooth device, received the answers at the examination and copied the said answers.

This information is confirmed through the technical information collected and thereby the said Shremant Satapur along with others has committed the NC:
2024:KHC-D:16482 offences punishable under Sections 109, 114, 120(B), 409, 420 read with Section 34, 36, 37, 149 IPC.
9.

Based on the complaint, the Dharwad Sub- Urban Police have registered the case and after detailed investigation filed charge sheet against accused Nos.1 to 3 for the offences punishable under Sections 120(B), 409, 420, 201 read with 34 and 37 of the IPC.

10. The Charge sheet reveal that accused No.1 in order to get through the selection of PSI post, he collected information to the effect that during the examination conducted by K.P.S.C. for the post of SDA, FDA, PWD Engineers, Teachers' post of Education Department, PSI, and constables examination conducted by the Police Department on payment of money accused No.2- Rudragowda Kashinath Hanumantaraya Chilla vs The State Of Karnataka on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82803110/
3 Patil, manages to get the answers through bluetooth device.

sentences.text: Accordingly, he met accused No.2- Rudragouda Patil.
He agreed to get the answers to accused No.1 through bluetooth device for payment of 40 lakh.
He received 10 lakh as advance.
Along with 10 NC: 2024:KHC-D:16482 lakh paid as advance.
As instructed by accused No.2, accused No.1 provided him with two sims and keypad mobile.
In turn, accused No.1 gave him a bluetooth device and instructed how to use it.
He also gave a white plain 'T' shirt and showed that there is a pocked below the color and advised him to keep the bluetooth device inside the said pocket and switch it on before entering the room.
After examination commences, his team would call him and give the answers.

After completion of the examination, he should return the bluetooth and 'T' shirt to accused No.2.
11.
To enable accused No.2 and his team to get all the questions papers, accused No.1 roped in accused No.3, who was working as a Principal in Jnyan Jyoti English Medium School, of Kalaburgi.

sentences.text: He was in a position to take all the administrative decisions, appoint teachers, change them and also appoint staff, disburse salary etc.
Accused No.3 was in close contact with accused No.1.

He agreed to help accused No.1 to get the photographs of all NC: 2024:KHC-D:16482 the question papers for both morning and afternoon examination and in this regard received 5 lakh.
12.

Accordingly, on the date of examination, accused No.3, collected the question papers of those candidates who did not attend the examination, took it inside his office and sent the photographs of all the question papers of both morning and afternoon examination to accused No.2.

In turn,
accused No.2 sent those question papers to his answering team and they sent the answers to accused No.1 through bluetooth device.
13. Initially, the accused persons were arrested in Kalburgi case.
So far as the present case is concerned, as evident from the order sheet dated 04.11.2022, the Investigating Officer has filed application to issue body warrant against accused Nos.2 and 3.
It was allowed and body warrant was issued against accused No.2 and 3 returnable by 10.11.2022.
It appears the office has not issued the body warrant against them and therefore, they - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:16482 were not produced before the Court on 10.11.2022.
Once again, the Investigating Officer has submitted requisition to issue body warrant against accused Nos.2 and 3.
The same was allowed and accused No.2 and 3 were ordered to be produced through body warrant on 28.11.2022.
14. Accordingly, on 28.11.2022, accused Nos.2 and 3 were produced before the Court through body warrant.
The Investigating Officer has sought for police custody.
The said application was allowed and accused Nos.2 and 3 were directed to be given to the police custody, till 03.12.2022.
In fact after conducting investigation based on the voluntary information given by accused Nos.2 and 3, the investigating officer has produced them before the Court on 01.12.2022 itself.
The trial Court has not chosen to extend their body warrant and simply sent them back to the judicial custody of the Court from which they were secured before it.

sentences.text: It appears accused No.3 has been granted regular bail in the original crime number in which he was in judicial custody.
Therefore, he is out of judicial custody and now seeking anticipatory bail.
Accordingly, he has approached the Sessions Court to grant the anticipatory bail.

However, the Sessions Court instead of examining whether petitioner is entitled for anticipatory bail or not, has simply dismissed the petition by observing that the trial Court has secured his presence through body warrant on 28.11.2022 and sent him to judicial custody on 31.11.2022 ( It should have been 01.12.2022).

16. As already noted, the trial Court has not at all extended the body warrant of accused Nos.2 and 3 before sending them back to the judicial custody of the Court, from which their presence was secured, so that after they were released on bail, in the original case, they could have been taken to the judicial custody of the trial Court.
Consequently, now the accused Nos.2 and 3 are neither on bail, nor they are in judicial custody, so far as present - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:16482 case is concerned.
Therefore, rightly the petitioner has sought anticipatory bail before the Sessions Court.
However, the Sessions Court has chosen to reject the petition, but not on merit.
Without any alternative, now the accused No.3 has approached this Court for grant of anticipatory bail.
17. Despite the fact that the allegations made against the petitioner are very grave, the trial Court has not chosen to keep the body warrant issued against him in force by extending it.
After taking the accused No.3 to the police custody, the Investigating Officer has conducted the investigation regarding his involvement in the present crime number.
Therefore, now the custodial presence of accused No.3 is also not required for investigation purpose.
In the above facts and circumstances, no purpose would serve by rejecting the request of accused No.3 for anticipatory bail.

Of course, the interest of the prosecution is required to be safeguarded by imposing stringent conditions, and accordingly the following;
- 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:16482 ORDER Petition is allowed.

Petitioner/accused No.3 shall be released on bail, in the event of his arrest in Crime No.216/2022 ( C.C.No.42/2023) pending on the file of Principal, Civil Judge and JMFC Dharwad, for the offences punishable under Sections 120(b), 409,
